notes: TugQL comment conformance vectors, shared by dal-go/dalgo (Go) and dal-go/dalgo-js (TypeScript). Both implementations must satisfy every case; yaml and roundTripText must match byte for byte.

Text form: `--` and `//` each start a comment that runs to the end of the line. They are recognised only outside string literals ('...') and quoted identifiers ("..." and `...`). `#` is NOT a comment in the text form.
Comment text: the characters after the marker with ONE leading space removed and trailing whitespace trimmed. `--x`, `-- x` and `// x` all carry the text `x`; `--` alone carries the empty text.

commentTokens: the lexer output for text, in source order. marker is the author's spelling; line and column are the 1-based position of the marker (columns count code points; the vectors use no characters outside the BMP); trailing is true when a token of the same line precedes the comment.

Anchors. A comment attaches to a clause-level element: `parameters`, `definitions[i]`, `query.from`, `query.from.joins[k]`, `query.from.joins[k].on[j]`, `query.where`, `query.groupBy`, `query.having`, `query.orderBy`, `query.limit`, `query.columns` (the SELECT clause). Comment lines above a clause are its leading comments; a comment after code on the clause's first line is its trailing comment.

No clean anchor: a comment on a continuation line of a multi-line clause (inside PARAMETERS, a WITH body, a multi-line SELECT block) and a comment on a YAML node that is not an anchor becomes a leading comment of the nearest FOLLOWING anchor; with no following anchor it becomes a document-end comment. A comment is never dropped.

Blank lines: a blank line between two comments of the same group is kept; a blank line before the first comment of a group, between the last comment and its element, or between the last code line and the document-end comments is not.

Structured YAML form: comments are `#` comments. A leading comment is the head comment above the clause key (or above the `- ` of a sequence item). A trailing comment is the same-line comment: after the scalar value when the clause value is a scalar (`limit: 5 # c`), after the key's colon when the value is a block (`from: # c`), and for a sequence item (join, on, definition) after the first entry of the item's mapping. An empty comment is a bare `#`. A blank line inside a comment block is an empty line. Document-end comments follow a blank line at the end of the document, one `# text` line per comment, with an empty line where blankBefore is set.

yaml bytes: the output of Go yaml.v3 yaml.Marshal with its default 4-space indentation. Key order: format, version, parameters, definitions, query; inside query: from, where, groupBy, having, orderBy, limit, columns. Scalars are plain except where YAML requires quoting; in particular the YAML 1.1 reserved word `on` is emitted double-quoted ("on") as a mapping key. The vectors avoid other quoting-sensitive scalars.

roundTripText: the text produced from yaml. It uses the canonical layout: lowercase keywords, no indentation except ON lines (two spaces), the SELECT list on one line, every comment spelled `--` (`-- ` + text, bare `--` for empty text). The `//` spelling is therefore lost on a text, YAML, text round trip: this is documented and accepted.
format: the output of the formatter for text with formatOptions (default options when empty), or null when text has diagnostics. The formatter keeps each comment's marker and text.

sql: for every case that parses, SQL emitted for any dialect from the query resolved against the top-level schema must not contain `//` outside string literals and quoted identifiers. Comments never reach SQL; an emitter that ever carries a comment writes it as `--`. stringLiterals and quotedIdentifiers list the only places `//` may legitimately appear.
yamlCases: structured YAML input to expected text. They also pin the reading rules: `--` inside a YAML scalar is not a comment, and `#` inside a quoted YAML scalar is not a comment.

textCases.name: leading-dash
textCases.description: A comment on its own line above a clause is the head comment of that clause.
textCases.text:
-- lead
from T
select Id

expected.format:
-- lead
from T
select Id
expected.yaml:
format: tugqtree
version: 1
query:
    # lead
    from:
        name: T
    columns:
        - field: Id
expected.roundTripText:
-- lead
from T
select Id

textCases.name: leading-and-trailing-on-clauses

where Id = 1 // on where
-- before select
select Id, Name

expected.format:
// lead
from T -- on from
where Id = 1 // on where
-- before select
select Id, Name
expected.yaml:
format: tugqtree
version: 1
query:
    # lead
    from: # on from
        name: T

        right:

        - field: Id
        - field: Name

-- lead
from T -- on from
where Id = 1 -- on where
-- before select
select Id, Name

    from:

        alias: t
        joins:
            # join lead
            - from: # join trail
                name: U
                alias: u
              "on":
                # on lead
                - op: == # on trail
                  left:
                    field: Id
                    source: t
                  right:
                    field: Id
                    source: u
    columns:

  -- on lead
